newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - March 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The sudden resignation of Sydney Organising Committee of the Olympic Games chief executive Dr Mal Hemmerling yesterday will be followed today by the confirmation that the A$344 million Sydney Olympic Stadium float has fallen short by A$200 million. The underwriting shortfall is one of the largest in the history of corporate Australia. Page 1.

Former Governor-General and Australian Labor Party leader Bill Hayden has warned the Howard Government should abolish native title over pastoral leases and ease the powers of Aboriginal claimants. Hayden believes failure to act on the High Court's decision will lead to Australia facing "economic detriment". Page 3.

It is believed the Australian Federal Police have given the Director of Public Prosecutions material relating to possible rorting charges against National Party backbencher Michael Cobb and former Liberal Senator Bob Woods. Police said yesterday their enquiries into both Cobb and Woods, which have been going since last year, are nearing completion. Page 3.

The Federal Government's decision last Friday, which sees the private sector not subject to enforceable national privacy codes, is at risk of backfiring and isolating Australia from international data flows. The European Union will next year ban the flow of data to any country that does not have adequate privacy laws in place. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Former Governor-General Bill Hayden has drawn on his experience with the Native Title Act as a negotiator in the Century Zinc mineral project to warn the Act is unreasonable, open to abuse and misuse and prone to generate jealously and mistrust. Hayden believes the Act will be economically damaging to Australia. Page 1.

Clerk of the Senate Harry Evans has advised the Federal Government the Australian Federal Police should be brought in to investigate claims of fraud against Independent Senator Mal Colston. However, Evans suggested that as the situation has political impications, further advice should be sought from Federal Attorney-General Daryl Williams. Page 1.

The Federal Government was accused of trying to complicate the republican debate through extended discussions and avoid a plebiscite yesterday as it introduced legislation calling for a 10-day convention in December that will only consider the republic and the head of State. The Government has dumped the discussion of other issues, such as the introduction of four-year parliamentary terms. Page 1.

A private meeting yesterday between Tasmanian Attorney-General Ray Groom and reformist Green MPs may result in the State's anti-gay laws being disbanded. It was expected a reform bill against the laws, which have been criticised internationally, would have been passed through the House of Assembly late last night. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales Olympics Minister Michael Knight has forced the resignation of Olympics chief Mal Hemmerling, following calls last week to members of the Organising Committee of the Sydney Olympics board to tell them his and Hemmerling's relationship could not continue and he would call for Hemmerling's resignation. Page 1.

Following the resignation of Papua New Guinean Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan yesterday, Australian Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer said he was happy with the way the crisis in the country was resolved, and that he believed the constitutional prcess if holding up. However, Downer conceded later that Australia had not paid enough attention to Papua New Guinea since it was granted independence in 1975. Page 1.

The Department of Community Services has come under fire following revelations that three children have been left in the care of their father, who last April was found guilty of two charges of sexual assault, and who has been psychologically assessed as a unfit parent. The children's foster parents are fighting to regain custody of the trio. Page 1.

Hamersley Iron Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of RTZ-CRA, last night endorsed the process of negotiating with Aboriginal people following the signing of an historic A$500 million agreement for a project in the West Australian Pilbara. The agreement is the first land use agreement for a major mine since the 1992 Mabo ruling. Page 1.
THE AGE

In an eight-page letter to Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge, former Governor-General Bill Hayden has criticised the high Court's Wik decision and claimed the native title process was confusing, complex, and leaving the way open for extortion claims by Aborginal people. Hayden warned problems must be fixed, or Australia will suffer serious economic damage. Page A1.

The Australian Football League season begins in earnest tonight at 7.40pm at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in a match between North Melbourne and Melbourne. The season is expected to differ greatly to last year's centenary season, with no sign of the mergers, power failures, galas and corporate movements that took some of the attention away from the field. Page A1.

The Federal Government has released plans for a convention on the republic that will only concentrate on the republic rather than taking a wide-ranging look at constitutional reform. In introducing legislation to set up the convention, Prime Minister John Howard said it would be held over 10 days in December, and only after it is held would the Government consider putting a referendum to the people. Page A3.

An estimated $12 million is owed to former Telstra employees that the company has been unable to locate. Poor records management has meant that back-pay owed to 20,000 employees is unable to be paid until a manual search of records back to 1987 has been completed. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
